Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT for Moira’s review — Light Up a Life 2026

Hilary Gotts asked on the page last week whether we would be doing the tree again, after her mum’s name was on it last year. Yes, Hilary, we are. I’m so glad it meant something to you, and we hope you and your sister will come.

Last year’s tree carried 412 names. Thank you to everyone who trusted us with one, and to those who stopped to read the tags, stood quietly for a while, or kept somebody company while they found the words. There was a great deal of love in this little shop, and we have not forgotten it.

It is seven years this month since Ray, my husband, died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag, I could hardly write his name. Now I write it here at the counter, with the same pen I used that first year. I can’t say it has become easy, exactly, but it has become something I can do among other people who understand that a name can take a little time.

I mention that because the tree is for anyone who is grieving. You do not need to have any connection with the hospice, and your loss does not have to be recent. Whoever you are remembering, and however long you have been remembering them, there is room for their name.

Memory tags will be in the shop from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. If you would rather write yours at home, there are envelopes on the counter. The tree goes into the window on Saturday 21 November.

We shall switch the lights on at 4pm on Saturday 28 November. The Gildencroft Primary choir are kindly coming back to sing three or four carols for us, and Doreen is making her mince pies again. Do come along if you can.

Once the tree is in the window, you are also very welcome simply to come in and stand beside it. You needn’t buy a book, or anything else, and you needn’t talk unless you want to. If a quiet minute with the names is what you need, that is quite enough.

Every name on the tags will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You do not have to attend the service for the name on your tag to be read. Whether you are there in person or not, they will be remembered.

I look forward to seeing some of you, and to hearing the children sing again.

Jean

reasons: The piece says the tree goes into the window on Saturday 21 November, but Moira's message says only 'the Saturday', most naturally the 28th when the lights go on, so the date is invented and may contradict it.
